text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet would make a statement on the current strength of the dollar on Wednesday.
"The cabinet will make a statement on this tomorrow," Waigel told Reuters, when asked to comment on the dollar on the sidelines of a European prize-giving ceremony in the Bavarian town of Dillingen.

Speaking earlier in Berlin, Waigel said Germany was interested in a strong mark, that markets had overreacted in pushing the dollar and sterling to multiple-year highs, and hinted that the Group of Seven (G7) could be prepared to take corrective action.

Waigel's support for the mark came hot on the heels of similar statements from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer last week but failed to hold the dollar back as it soared to 71-month highs above 1.80 marks.

Analysts blamed the mark's weakness on a simmering row in Germany over how strictly entry criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) should be interpreted. They said this had discredited both the planned euro and the mark itself.

The G7 industrialised nations, which in 1995 called for an "orderly reversal" of the dollar from record lows near 1.3450 marks, signalled in February at a dollar rate of about 1.65 marks that the recovery had gone about far enough.
